title: Clustered customer feedback narratives and prioritized asks — Oct 2026
summary: This note turns ~120 raw CS threads (May-Sep 2026) into six narrative clusters and a recommended action slate. It emphasizes product experiments that reduce failed rollouts and unexpected cost spikes for Dedicated and Private customers. The goal is pragmatic: propose 3 quick wins and 2 investigative projects that the product and engineering teams can scope within the next quarter.
methodology: Sourced 118 threads from Zendesk and internal CS Slack triage (filtered for paid Dedicated/Private customers). Performed rapid affinity clustering to group similar asks and extracted representative verbatim quotes. Each cluster was scored by frequency, operational risk, and business impact. Prioritization applied a 3-factor rubric: customer pain (severity), breadth (# customers), and implementation complexity (engineering estimate).
themes: Cluster A — Predictable latency degradation during sustained batch loads: Frequency=High. Representative quote: 'Latency spikes after 30 minutes of continuous traffic—timeouts and then a long warmup.' Impact: production outages and customer churn risk for PLG -> Enterprise. Suggested fix: server-side adaptive batching cap + soft throttling policy and explicit quota notifications. Priority: P0-P1 depending on customer SLA. Estimated effort: Medium (serving-runtime + routing policy).

Cluster B — Lack of clear model variant fallbacks and explanation: Frequency=Medium-High. Representative quote: 'We got silently downgraded to a quantized variant and lost answer fidelity; no audit trail.' Impact: trust & compliance issues for regulated workflows. Suggested fix: expose fallback policy logs in Console and add 'why-fallback' explanation to request traces. Priority: P1. Estimated effort: Low-Medium (console UX + tracing hooks).

Cluster C — Embedding drift and incompatibility between model versions: Frequency=Medium. Representative quote: 'Embeddings from v1.2 and v1.3 are not comparable—semantic search quality regressed.' Impact: broken pipelines for customers using long-term embeddings store. Suggested fix: semantic-versioning for embeddings, stable migration tooling, and automated similarity regression tests. Priority: P1-P2. Estimated effort: Medium-High (embedding infra + docs).

Cluster D — Confusing billing spikes tied to KV cache misses and prefix expansion: Frequency=Medium. Representative quote: 'Monthly bill doubled after we enabled conversation caching—we don't understand the token math.' Impact: revenue churn and support load. Suggested fix: add cost simulation in Console (per-route cost preview), clearer docs, and a console toggle to limit unbounded prefix caching. Priority: P0 for customers with spend > threshold. Estimated effort: Low-Medium (console + docs).

Cluster E — Private deployment onboarding friction: VPN/KMS/Firewall choreography: Frequency=Medium-Low. Representative quote: 'The network setup took three weeks and required infra tickets on our side.' Impact: sales cycle elongation for regulated customers. Suggested fix: create a prescriptive onboarding runbook, Terraform module examples, and a short managed-onboarding service offering. Priority: P2 for self-serve, P0-P1 for sales-assisted deals. Estimated effort: Low (docs + templates) to Medium (service).

Cluster F — Observability gaps for per-request quality regressions: Frequency=Low-Medium. Representative quote: 'We can't correlate prompt changes to small quality regressions across model variants.' Impact: silent regression risk and lengthy root-cause investigations. Suggested fix: tie eval prompt sets to production routes and add drift alerts with sample-level diffing. Priority: P1. Estimated effort: Medium (console + monitoring integration).

cross_cutting_risks: Silent fallbacks and lack of clear telemetry can erode trust faster than raw latency issues—customers report losing faith if they cannot trace why a change happened.
Cost surprises are disproportionately harmful for mid-market customers on Dedicated capacity; they trigger rapid deprovisioning and churn.
On-prem and VPC customers expect battle-tested onboarding artifacts; repeated manual steps increase sales friction and SOW complexity.
Instrumenting more telemetry increases observability but also raises privacy/compliance questions for regulated customers—need KMS/HSM alignment and data retention guardrails.
top_actions: Action 1 — Quick win: Add a 'Why was this request routed/fallbacked?' panel in the Console traces. Owner: Product-Console (Sofia). ETA: 4 weeks. Rationale: Low engineering cost, high trust improvement for Cluster B.

Action 2 — Quick win: Cost preview UI for per-route prefix/caching settings. Owner: Product-Console + Billing (Liam). ETA: 6 weeks. Rationale: Directly addresses billing spikes (Cluster D) and reduces CS ticket load.

Action 3 — Experiment: Adaptive batching cap pilot for 3 Dedicated customers experiencing latency degradation. Owner: Serving Runtime (Jordan). ETA: 8 weeks for pilot + metrics dashboard. Rationale: High-impact for Cluster A; measurable SLO improvement likely.

Action 4 — Investigation: Embedding versioning policy and migration patterns. Owner: Applied ML + Product (Aisha). ETA: research report in 6 weeks then roadmap item. Rationale: Prevents long-running pipeline regressions (Cluster C).

Action 5 — Enablement: Private deployment onboarding bundle (Terraform templates, runbook, checklist). Owner: Solutions Engineering. ETA: 3 weeks for templates. Rationale: Shortens sales cycle and reduces professional services lift (Cluster E).
impact_and_effort_notes: Scoring highlights: Cluster A and D are highest immediate business risk because they correlate with outages and billing churn; treat them as P0/P1 for customers with Defined SLAs.
Many asks can be addressed with improved Console UX + small telemetry additions rather than large runtime rewrites—prioritize these for 30–60 day wins.
Longer-term investments (embeddings compatibility, drift detection) require roadmap slots and cross-team ownership between Applied ML, Serving Runtime, and Console.
recommended_next_steps: Share this note with Eng-Serving-Runtime, Product-Console, and Applied-ML in the Oct 15 cross-functional triage meeting.
Create JIRA epics for the three quick wins and tag affected accounts for pilot programs.
Design a lightweight CS-facing playbook to triage billing spike tickets within 24 hours and escalate to an on-call product engineer if above spend threshold.
